title: Air
tagline: Nike had one shot at Michael Jordan.
about: In 1984 Nike's basketball scout bets the company's whole basketball budget on signing a rookie called Michael Jordan.

Crisp rolled tortillas with beef chilli and cheese.How to make it400g beef mince1 brown onion, finely diced2 tsp ground cumin2 tsp chilli powder200g tomato passata150g tasty cheese, grated12 small corn tortillas3 tbsp olive oil200g sour cream200g tomato salsaBrown the mince with the onion, then add the cumin, chilli and passata and simmer until thick.Warm the tortillas so they bend, then fill each with chilli and cheese and roll up tight.Brush with oil and bake seam-side down at 220°C until crisp.Serve with sour cream and salsa.High roller prawn cocktailSonny's big win at the Vegas tables. Cold king prawns in Marie Rose sauce on iceberg.How to make it500g cooked king prawns, peeled1/2 iceberg lettuce, finely shredded5 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 lemon, cut in wedges1/2 tsp sweet paprika1 avocado, dicedStir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, Worcestershire and a squeeze of lemon together.Fill 4 coupes with lettuce and avocado.Pile on the prawns, spoon over the sauce and dust with paprika.Serve cold with lemon wedges.Hot lineWilmington vinegar pulled porkSonny visits Deloris in Wilmington. Carolina vinegar pork and slaw in soft white rolls.How to make it1.5kg pork shoulder, boneless2 tbsp brown sugar2 tsp smoked paprika250ml apple cider vinegar1 tsp chilli flakes1 tbsp tomato sauce8 soft white rolls1/4 green cabbage, finely shredded3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaiseRub the pork with the sugar, paprika and salt and sit it in a lidded pot with 250ml water.Cover and cook at 160°C until it pulls apart easily.Shake the vinegar, chilli flakes and tomato sauce together, then pull the pork and toss it through.Dress the cabbage with the mayo and a splash of the sauce and pile into the rolls with the pork.Olympic coach's steak fritesSonny asks George Raveling over dinner. Grilled sirloin with fries and pepper sauce.How to make it4 x 250g sirloin steaks1kg floury potatoes, cut in chips3 tbsp olive oil30g butter1 French shallot, finely diced1 tbsp cracked black pepper200ml thickened cream1 tbsp Dijon mustardBoil the chips for 5 minutes, drain, toss with 2 tbsp oil and roast at 220°C until crisp.Season the steaks and sear in the remaining oil to your liking, then rest.In the same pan melt the butter, soften the shallot, add the pepper, cream and mustard and bubble until thick.Serve the steaks with the fries and sauce.SweetsAir Jordan red velvet cakePeter Moore names the shoe Air Jordan. Red velvet layers with cream cheese and dark chocolate.How to make it250g plain flour2 tbsp cocoa powder1 tsp bicarbonate of soda250g caster sugar250ml neutral oil2 eggs250ml buttermilk1 tbsp red food colouring1 tsp white vinegar250g cream cheese, soft100g butter, soft300g icing sugar100g dark chocolate, finely gratedWhisk the flour, cocoa, bicarb and sugar, then beat in the oil, eggs, buttermilk, colouring and vinegar.Split between 2 lined 20cm tins and bake at 175°C until a skewer comes out clean, then cool.Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until fluffy.Sandwich and cover the cakes with the icing and press the grated chocolate around the sides.DrinksEvery pair sold old fashionedDeloris wants a cut of every shoe sold.
